author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Wildcard Accept-Encoding does not enable Brotli.
findings.consequence: Requests such as `Accept-Encoding: gzip, *;q=1` are Brotli-capable by HTTP content negotiation, but the production caller will leave eligible HTML uncompressed because only explicit `br` tokens are accepted.
findings.evidence: Line 17 returns false for every token whose coding is not exactly `br`; there is no later branch for `*`. The direct caller at server/plugins/response-compression.ts:63 uses this boolean as the sole gate before setting `Content-Encoding: br`. The named unit tests cover explicit `br` and `q=0` cases at test/unit/response-compression.spec.ts:118-135 but do not cover wildcard negotiation.
findings.recommendation: Track explicit `br` and wildcard qualities while preserving explicit `br;q=0` precedence; return true when `br` has positive quality or when no `br` token is present and `*` has positive quality. Add unit and production negotiation tests for `*;q=1`, `gzip, *;q=0`, and `br;q=0, *;q=1`.
